data.title: ddflow/services/export/region_check.py:19 (`_parsed`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_parsed` short-circuits on `_MARK in text`, i.e. it skips `RG.parse` entirely whenever the literal substring `ddflow:begin` does not occur, and returns `[]` — which is exactly the "no regions, nothing to report" answer rather than the "markers unreadable" answer. So a hand-edit that removes the begin marker line (`<!-- ddflow:begin doc/page <hash> -->`) while leaving the matching `<!-- ddflow:end doc/page -->` in place — a common botched merge-conflict resolution — turns into silence: `problem()` returns `""` and `edited()` returns `[]`, so the pre-commit check and the doctor note both read the file as a clean whole-file document and let it through. An orphaned end marker is the textbook "unbalanced" marker case the module docstring promises is reported by `problem`, and the body hash can no longer be checked at all once the begin marker is gone. `mask()` has the same hop (it returns `_parsed()`, so a `RegionError` path is never reached here either), leaving the leftover template lines in the text docscheck prose-checks. The guard should only elide the no-marker-at-all case (which `RG.parse` already answers with `[]`); as written it also elides the malformed case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/region_check.py:19 (`_parsed`)

chunk_findings.detail:
`_parsed` now returns `[]` for the *entire document* as soon as one adopt-stamped block is found anywhere in it: `any(m in text for m in _MARKS) and not _STAMPED.search(text)`. A file that legitimately contains both an adopt-stamped block and a real generated region therefore stops being parsed at all. Concretely, given

```
<!-- ddflow:begin rules/work-queue ddflow=0.2.0 fmt=1 sha=f60922c1c1f6 -->
x
<!-- ddflow:end rules/work-queue -->
<!-- ddflow:begin doc/page deadbeef -->
hand-edited body
<!-- ddflow:end doc/page -->
```

`_STAMPED.search` matches the first line, so `problem(text)` returns `""` and `edited(...)` returns `[]` — the hand-edited `doc/page` region is exactly the thing the pre-commit enforcement is supposed to refuse, and it is silently accepted; the hash check is bypassed for that file. The same short-circuit breaks the other direction for `mask`: an unstamped-but-real region's generated body is left in the text, so `docscheck` prose-checks generated region content it was meant to exclude, producing false findings, while the stamped block is (correctly) skipped. The previous code (`_MARK in text`) did parse such a mixed document; this change regresses it by keying the decision off the presence of any stamped block rather than off the region under inspection. The `_STAMPED` check needs to be per-region (or the stamped lines excised/neutralized before `RG.parse`), not a whole-text veto. Note also that a stamped-looking line inside a fenced code example in an otherwise real region-bearing doc triggers the same whole-file silence.
